h1: The One Hotel Bueng Kan — the city hotel travellers passing through book again
intro: Bueng Kan is Thailand's smallest and newest province, so options with a pool and full facilities in town are few · The One Hotel is the name that comes up most often for a city stay in Bueng Kan · It sits on the Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Road, right next to Lotus and within walking distance · Open since 2010 and given a major renovation in 2022, it has 79 rooms, an outdoor pool with a water slide, a gym, a breakfast buffet and free parking — from around ฿1,100/night · Real guest reviews score it as high as 9.1, ranking it among the top hotels in town.

body.html: The One Hotel has been open since 2010 and is one of the most familiar city hotels to Bueng Kan residents · It sits on the Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Road in Tambon Bueng Kan, right next to Lotus for easy shopping · A major renovation in 2022 left it feeling fresher than its age suggests · This is not a design-led boutique stay — it's a 79-room city hotel with everything a guest passing through or on business in Bueng Kan needs · In a province where options like this are scarce, The One stands out as the first name many people think of.

Rooms range from Superior Twin/Queen up to Deluxe and Grand Deluxe Queen · What guests consistently praise is that rooms are more spacious than expected and clean, with comfortable beds, cold air-con, a flatscreen TV, a fridge and free Wi-Fi · Many reviews note the rooms feel larger than the price · The trade-offs: some rooms have reports of inconsistent shower-temperature control and a little mould around the sink or shower in places — if you hit it, flag it or ask to switch, as reviews say staff are helpful.
"The room was really spacious and clean, the bed comfy, and the staff were lovely and spoke English · Breakfast had made-to-order omelettes too — at this price in Bueng Kan it's hard to find better."

What sets The One apart from a typical city hotel is its outdoor pool with a water slide and a separate children's pool, a big hit with families travelling with kids · There's a gym and a restaurant serving Thai food and a breakfast buffet · Breakfast earns praise for the made-to-order eggs/omelettes and a varied Thai spread · Worth noting: Western options are limited and the restaurant isn't open for dinner every day · There's ample free parking and EV charging, which is rare in this province.

Location is the main reason people choose it · It's on the Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Road, right next to Lotus and walkable · The town centre and the Mekong riverfront are a short drive away, making it handy for business and government visits, or as a base for the Naka Cave, Phu Tok and the province's waterfalls · The hotel can help with transfers and travel arrangements · Be aware that Bueng Kan is a small town — nights are quiet and there isn't much going on right around the hotel, so most people use it as a base and drive out to explore.

To be honest, per real guest sentiment: The One is listed as 4-star on some platforms, but in practice it's closer to a good city hotel than a luxury property · Some reviews mention fairly firm beds, missing in-room items like tea/coffee/cups at times, loaner bicycles without locks, and a few non-functional lights on the front sign · Guests who are disappointed usually expected a luxury resort, while those who understand they're booking one of the best hotels in a small province tend to be very satisfied — reflected in the 9.1 score and the #1-of-5 ranking among Bueng Kan City hotels on TripAdvisor.

In short, if you want a stay in central Bueng Kan with a pool, clean and spacious rooms, breakfast, free parking and a location next to the mall — and you're not expecting resort-level luxury — The One delivers and is the safest pick in town · It suits families with kids (thanks to the slide), business travellers, and anyone using Bueng Kan as a base for the Naka Cave and Phu Tok.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a renovated room when booking or at check-in, as room condition isn't consistent throughout · Pack your own tea/coffee sachets and a small cup in case the room is missing them · And if you're travelling with kids, leave time in the evening for the pool slide — it's the highlight here for younger guests.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The One Hotel Bueng Kan

faq.q: Where is The One Hotel in Bueng Kan, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The One Hotel is at 459 Moo 1, Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Road, Tambon Bueng Kan, in downtown Bueng Kan · It's next to Lotus and within walking distance · The town centre and Mekong riverfront are a few minutes' drive · It's about a 45-minute drive to Phu Tok and around 1 hour to the Naka Cave (Phu Langka National Park).

faq.q: How much does The One Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿1,100/night for a Superior Twin/Queen · A Deluxe Queen runs about ฿1,350 and a Grand Deluxe Queen around ฿1,600 · Prices vary by date and platform — compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does The One Hotel have a pool, and is it good for families?
faq.a: Yes — there's an outdoor pool with a water slide and a separate kids' pool that reviews praise as family-friendly · There's also a gym and a breakfast buffet · It's one of the few stays in Bueng Kan town with a pool like this.

faq.q: Is The One Hotel really a 4-star hotel?
faq.a: Some platforms like Agoda/Booking list it as 4-star · But per real guest reviews, the condition and service are closer to a good city hotel than a luxury resort · Even so, it's one of the best hotels in Bueng Kan town (ranked #1 of 5 on TripAdvisor), with a 9.1 score from 58 Trip.com reviews.

faq.q: Who is The One Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for business visitors to Bueng Kan, families with kids (thanks to the pool slide), and travellers using Bueng Kan as a base for the Naka Cave, Phu Tok or the riverfront · Free parking and EV charging make it good for self-drivers · It's not for those after a luxury resort or a lively nightlife area.

faq.q: What's breakfast like at The One Hotel?
faq.a: Breakfast is a made-to-order buffet with omelettes/fried eggs and a varied Thai spread that reviews praise · Note that Western options are limited and the restaurant isn't open for dinner every day — check ahead if you plan to dine in.
